title: Superadiabatic Dynamical Density Functional Theory for One-Dimensional Brownian Hard-Rod Fluids
authors: Jens Weimar, Daniel de las Heras, Martin Oettel
abstract: We study the relaxation dynamics of a one-dimensional system of hard rods at the level of one-body fields using superadiabatic dynamical density functional theory, and compare the results with Brownian dynamics simulations. The theory uses the exact equilibrium excess free energy functional and incorporates superadiabatic effects from first principles via an adiabatic closure relation at the three-particle level. The predicted superadiabatic response shows very good agreement with simulation data, provided that initial-state ensemble differences between theory and simulations remain small. Furthermore, we evaluate an approximate power functional theory based on a velocity-gradient expansion, which also yields an accurate superadiabatic response, although requiring a memory kernel extracted from simulation data.
summary: This work develops and validates Superadiabatic Dynamical Density Functional Theory (SDDFT) for modeling the relaxation dynamics of 1D hard-rod fluids. By incorporating superadiabatic effects beyond the standard adiabatic approximation, SDDFT achieves quantitative agreement with Brownian Dynamics simulations. The study highlights the critical role of non-adiabatic terms in accurately describing non-equilibrium transport in soft matter systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately describing the non-equilibrium relaxation dynamics of interacting fluids, specifically focusing on capturing superadiabatic effects beyond standard adiabatic approximations.
main_result: Superadiabatic Dynamical Density Functional Theory (SDDFT) shows excellent quantitative agreement with Brownian Dynamics simulations for the total current, suggesting it correctly captures non-adiabatic memory effects.
method: The authors employ advanced theoretical frameworks like SDDFT and Power Functional Theory (PFT), comparing them against molecular dynamics simulations.
model_or_system: The system studied is a one-dimensional (1D) fluid composed of hard rods, whose dynamics are modeled using the Smoluchowski equation. The theory builds upon classical DFT by incorporating higher-order correlations up to the three-particle level.
key_observables: One-body density profile ($ho(r, t)$), total current ($j_{tot}$), adiabatic current ($j_{ad}$), and superadiabatic current ($j_{sup}$).
important_parameters: The comparison is sensitive to ensemble differences (canonical vs. grand canonical) and the degree of superadiabaticity.
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve the closure relations used in SDDFT (at the three-particle level) and the functional ansatz used in PFT. A major limitation noted is the discrepancy arising from ensemble mismatch.
figures_summary: Figures compare the time evolution of the total current ($j_{tot}$) and its components ($j_{ad}, j_{sup}$) across DDFT, SDDFT, PFT, and BD simulations, highlighting the success of SDDFT.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops SDDFT by extending DDFT to include three-particle correlations. It then compares this result against PFT and benchmark BD simulations, analyzing the contributions of the adiabatic and superadiabatic currents.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluids, the rigorous development of non-equilibrium dynamics using density functionals and the explicit separation of adiabatic vs. non-adiabatic (superadiabatic) contributions provides a powerful methodological template applicable to open quantum systems where memory effects are crucial.
